response.text:
The verifier says the group must net to zero per account, which implies the correction should reverse the original lines. My first attempt reversed and then re-booked the entries, but the 1200 net came out at -2691.14. The re-booked 1200 line had the wrong side: the original is CR 1200, so the re-book should also be CR, and I had written that correctly. The reversal was wrong, though. The reversal line for 1200 should be a DR, and I had that correctly too.

Counting the lines, the net came out as: original CR 2691.14, reversal DR 2691.14, re-book CR 2691.14, which leaves a net credit of 2691.14, and that is the -2691.14 the verifier reported. Re-booking therefore leaves the group with the accrual still in force, so it does not net to zero.

The verifier expects the original lines plus my lines to net to zero for every account. The simplest correction is a pure reversal in open period 11, which keeps the correction as small as the finding allows. Because the original is in a closed period, the reversal is posted in the open period.

arguments.reasoning: Manual accrual journal 2463 (JSMITH) was posted on 20240808 into period 7, which closed on 20240805. Posted rows cannot be edited and a closed period cannot be posted to, so a new journal in open period 11 fully reverses the original lines (CR 5100 5382.28, DR 2100 2691.14, DR 1200 2691.14). The original plus the correction nets to zero on every account and balances. No invoice status changes.
